prompt: Our team got breached through our API gateway and a cloud key was stolen. Can you audit all our infra repos and tell us where we're still vulnerable?
We just upgraded LiteLLM after that SQL injection advisory. Verify the fix is actually live on our production endpoint.
I want to reproduce the CVE-2026-42208 attack chain locally to prove to my team our old deployment was really exploitable.
Check whether the master key in our SOPS-encrypted env file was ever rotated after the incident last month.
Write up the security findings from this audit as individual reports with severity, affected files, and proposed fixes, plus an executive summary.
Diff our prod and staging gateway configs — I suspect prod is missing a hardening flag that staging has.
Someone reported a GHSA against a pinned dependency in our docker image. Figure out if our deployed version is actually affected and what the exposure window was.
Fire the payloads that worked before the patch at our live endpoint to confirm they're blocked now. We own the endpoint and authorize the test.
Build a vulnerable test environment in Docker so we can A/B test our old image against the patched one with the same payloads.
Did we leave any secrets in the git history of this deployment repo, and is anything still unrotated since the breach?
Full security review please: repos, deployment configs, and the live endpoints. We want per-finding reports at the end.
Our audit found six issues. Turn the findings ledger into a report set — one file per finding and an exec summary indexing them.
Bump our locked dependencies to clear the Dependabot alerts on the lockfile.
A GHSA was published for a package we use. Walk the lockfile -> CI cache -> secrets -> persistence check for it.
Harden our GitHub Actions workflows: pin actions to SHAs and set minimal permissions.
Add an SBOM and Sigstore signing to our release pipeline.
Scan our Docker images for vulnerabilities with Trivy and set up the scan in CI.
Set up password authentication with JWT tokens for our Flask app.
Why is my docker-compose service failing its healthcheck on startup?
Review this PR for code quality and style issues.
